body: @rclone/rclone Do any rclone developers have a mac and would like to help with this?

> Do any rclone developers have a mac and would like to help with this?

I can have a look into it

Although I remember reading a while ago that the future of FUSE on macOS would be uncertain: the main reason being that Apple is removing kernel extensions in the next release of macOS (this autumn). It's going to be replaced by kernel hooks.

I don't know if anybody is working on porting FUSE into kernel hooks right now, and don't even know if it's actually possible, but it looks like the way we use FUSE on macOS is going to change anyway

I cross-compiled with `--tags cmount` using the `billzissxgo-cgofuse` docker image on my Linux machine,
then I tried to run it on a Mac with no OSXFUSE installed, and ... yeah it doesn't like it:

```
% ./rclone-darwin-10.6-amd64
dyld: Library not loaded: /usr/local/lib/libosxfuse_i64.2.dylib
  Referenced from: ./rclone-darwin-10.6-amd64
  Reason: image not found
zsh: abort      ./rclone-darwin-10.6-amd64
```

...and it runs perfectly on my other Mac with OSXFUSE installed

Thanks for giving that a go, that is probably what I expected ☹️

What we need is a recipe for partially linking the macOS build as described here: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/26492#issuecomment-525527016

I've made the fully static build work for Linux. That might work for macOS too but isn't recommended, hence the desire to statically link osxfuse but not the standard libraries.

I don't really want to make osxfuse a dependency of rclone so we either need to do the linking trick, supply two binaries or abandon cmount on macOS.

Have you tried rclone mount2 on your Mac? It works in the CI that is as much as I know! That is the other option.

> Have you tried rclone mount2 on your Mac? It works in the CI that is as much as I know! That is the other option.

Good point.
Well, I just tried and it doesn't work:
- when running as a normal user it says permission denied.
- running with sudo, it looks like it mounts something, but you can't access it, and you can't unmount it.

Then I tried cmount, and it worked perfectly. I did a rsync on a mounted folder from my seafile server without any issue.

Quite annoying to say the least :thinking: 

> Apple seem to be making life harder for open source development.

I'm actually thinking giving up Mac and start working full time on Linux...

Can you see if there is a `.a` file in the download you get from OSXFUSE - I tried to unpack it but got stuck on linux! If there isn't a `.a` but only a `dll` or `.so` (whatever they are called on `macOS` then we'll have no alternative but to go for the two binary approach.)

Just a thought, rclone could do what git does - when you type `git command` if there is a command called `git-command` in the path then git will run it. So we could make an `rclone` without mount and another `rclone-mount` with mount which would be invoked by `rclone mount`.

You mean once installed on the mac? I'm not sure I can open the installer (.pkg file) to poke around otherwise.
Once installed, I can find only one file of interest:

```
$ file /Library/Frameworks/OSXFUSE.framework/OSXFUSE
OSXFUSE: Mach-O universal binary with 4 architectures: [ppc_7400:Mach-O dynamically linked shared library ppc_7400] [x86_64:Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library x86_64]
OSXFUSE (for architecture ppc7400):	Mach-O dynamically linked shared library ppc_7400
OSXFUSE (for architecture ppc64):	Mach-O dynamically linked shared library ppc64
OSXFUSE (for architecture i386):	Mach-O dynamically linked shared library i386
OSXFUSE (for architecture x86_64):	Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library x86_64
```

> Just a thought, rclone could do what git does - when you type `git command` if there is a command called `git-command` in the path then git will run it. So we could make an `rclone` without mount and another `rclone-mount` with mount which would be invoked by `rclone mount`.

I like this approach :)

>Once installed, I can find only one file of interest:

All those are dynamically linked so we can't static link them.

So it looks like the choices are two binaries with cmount or fixing up mount2.

The two binaries trick would work for all supported oses...

We know for now cmount works fine (at least on one I've tested) so maybe we can try to go this route first?

For the long run, that would be ideal if we could work out why mount2 wasn't working, that would mean only one library to maintain...

cmount is required for windows so with mount2 we still need two libraries ☹️

I'd really like to use cmount/cgofuse everywhere.

Under Windows cgofuse dynamically loads the dll so you don't need to link with the fuse DLL and rclone runs without WinFSP installed. I wonder if that trick is possible with Linux & macOS. That would be a nice solution.

@billziss-gh is it possible to delay the loading of the dll under macOS and Linux in cgofuse like the Windows version does?

> @billziss-gh is it possible to delay the loading of the dll under macOS and Linux in cgofuse like the Windows version does?

@ncw I have not attempted it before, but it should be possible to `dlopen` the FUSE dylib/so and `dlsym` the necessary symbols on demand.

The question is of course whether we are doing this from C (cgo) or Go. It is of course possible in C, but last time I checked Go did not support a general form of `dlopen` (things may have changed). (**EDIT**: Unfortunately golang/go#18296 is still open, so it would seem that our only option would be to do this from cgo.)

If this is the only option left on macOS, let me know and I will put some more time in cgofuse. Currently I am wrestling with getting FUSE mounts to work on WSL1. I have got a FUSE driver for WSL1 loading and functional, but mounting has proven more of a challenge than I expected.
